name: Marsha Blackburn
bio: Tennessee's senior U.S. senator since 2019, Blackburn is the polling frontrunner with broad establishment support and statewide name recognition. Trump-aligned conservative.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Blackburn's governor campaign does not include a specific early childhood education or pre-K expansion proposal. Her education platform centers on school choice expansion, parental rights, and opposing what she calls 'woke' curriculum.
early_childhood_ed.details: Blackburn's campaign website lists issues including 'Strengthening Parental Rights,' 'Fighting Woke Anti-American Curriculum,' and 'Improving Higher Education and Vocational Training,' but contains no page or statement on pre-K, Head Start, or early childhood education. In January 2026, she publicly called for the Tennessee legislature to expand the Education Freedom Scholarships voucher program, saying 'no parent should have to win the lottery to have a say in their child's education.' A bill pushing universal pre-K funding (SB 2512/HB 2008) failed in the Tennessee Senate in March 2026 with no Blackburn involvement noted. Her federal record reflects consistent opposition to federally directed early education programs and support for school choice mechanisms instead.

child_hunger.summary: Blackburn co-sponsored legislation to maintain SNAP funding during a government shutdown and publicly praised a 2026 SNAP waiver restricting junk food purchases in Tennessee, framing it as a health improvement rather than a cut to food assistance.
child_hunger.details: In October 2025, Blackburn co-sponsored the Keep SNAP Funded Act to ensure uninterrupted SNAP benefits during a government shutdown, stating 'roughly one in 10 Tennesseans receive SNAP benefits and they shouldn't have to worry about where their next meal will come from.' In January 2026, she praised the USDA-approved waiver restricting SNAP from being used for soda and sugary foods in Tennessee starting July 31, 2026, thanking Governor Lee and federal health officials. The Working Families Tax Cuts she championed shifted SNAP administrative costs from a 50-50 federal-state split to a 75% state share, creating additional budget pressures on Tennessee. No Blackburn statements on Summer EBT or the Tennessee SUN Bucks legislative debate were found.

parental_support.summary: Blackburn championed the Working Families Tax Cuts (the signed One Big Beautiful Bill), securing a permanently enhanced Child Tax Credit at $2,200 per child, an expanded employer childcare tax credit, and a permanent Paid Family and Medical Leave Tax Credit. She opposes government-mandated paid leave or federally administered childcare programs.
parental_support.details: The Working Families Tax Cuts permanently set the Child Tax Credit at $2,200 per child, indexed for inflation. Blackburn personally secured an expansion of the Employer-Provided Child Care Credit, citing that 48% of Tennessee residents live in childcare deserts, and the law raised the employer childcare credit maximum to $500,000 ($600,000 for small businesses). The law also permanently expanded the Paid Family and Medical Leave Tax Credit nationwide, reduced the minimum employment requirement from one year to six months, and established Trump Accounts — tax-advantaged savings accounts with a $1,000 Treasury seed for children born 2025–2028. In a February 2026 Senate floor speech, Blackburn called the law 'historic tax relief' and in an April 2026 op-ed noted the enhanced child tax credit had been claimed by more than 34 million families.

name: John Rose
bio: Four-term congressman from the Cumberland Plateau leaving his House seat to run. Farmer and small-business owner from Cookeville.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: Rose's governor campaign platform focuses on K-12 school choice, parental choice, classical education rooted in Tennessee values, and Career and Technical Education. He has pledged to appoint a Commissioner of Education who has actually taught in a Tennessee public school classroom. No position on early childhood education, pre-K, Head Start, or childcare programs has been found.
early_childhood_ed.details: In a May 21, 2026 radio interview on Mix 104.1, Rose stated: 'While supporting parental choice, Rose emphasized that 89% of Tennessee children graduate from public schools, making public education a top priority. He advocated for a curriculum rooted in classical education and Tennessee values, and pledged to appoint a Commissioner of Education with actual experience teaching in a state public school classroom.' At a May 30 Sparta meet-and-greet, he repeated: 'If you elect me, we will have a Commissioner of Education that has spent time teaching in a public-school classroom.' A May 18 ProEdTN interview characterized his priorities as: recognizing state educational gains, recruiting/retaining teachers through better compensation, strengthening local control, and school safety. None address children below kindergarten age. No pre-K or childcare content found.

child_hunger.summary: No specific position on child hunger, SNAP, Summer EBT, or school nutrition programs has been found in Rose's governor campaign. His campaign platform does not address food security policy.
child_hunger.details: Rose's campaign website and available 2026 news coverage contain no statements on SNAP, Summer EBT/SUN Bucks, school meals, or food assistance for children. In his February 2026 Knox News interview, he mentioned 'children's services, how we care for the most vulnerable in our society' as issues heard on the campaign trail, but offered no specific policy positions. As a U.S. Representative, Rose voted yes on the Nutritious SNAP Act of 2025, but he resigned from Congress to focus on the governor race and no new votes or statements on food assistance have been identified since. Tennessee's ongoing Summer EBT legislative debate has not drawn any public comment from Rose.

parental_support.summary: Rose's campaign has no identified positions on paid family leave, child tax credit, or childcare affordability. His family-focused platform language centers on protecting children from 'woke indoctrination' and gender ideology, not on financial support programs for parents.
parental_support.details: The 'Protect Tennessee Kids and Families' section of Rose's campaign website addresses opposition to gender transition treatments for minors and 'woke indoctrination' in schools, but does not mention paid family leave, child tax credits, childcare costs, or any parental financial support programs. In campaign appearances through May 2026, including a Lincoln Day Dinner speech and his 'Tough Like Trump' ad launch, Rose has emphasized faith, family, freedom, CEO experience, and constitutional rights, with no mention of family economic support policies. Rose received a 100% rating from the Family Research Council in February 2026, an organization focused on social conservative family values rather than family economic support.

name: Monty Fritts
bio: East Tennessee state legislator running on a populist conservative platform. Lower profile statewide than Blackburn or Rose.
photo_credit: No headshot found at direct image URL; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific position on early childhood education, pre-K, Head Start, or childcare programs. Fritts' platform explicitly opposes taxpayer-funded vouchers (Education Freedom Scholarships) — a significant distinction from the other Republican governors — and favors strengthening public education instead.
early_childhood_ed.details: fritts4tn.com is now live with a full 10-plank 'Liberty & Less Government' platform. Plank 3 ('Save Education, Respect Parents') states: 'Parents are the first and final voice in their children's education. Preserve Tennessee values and traditions in every classroom. Put reading, writing, math, and civics ahead of ideology. Respect teachers who respect the family.' A May 18, 2026 interview with Professional Educators of Tennessee confirmed: 'He supports parental choice but opposes taxpayer-funded vouchers, a defining position. He argues that public dollars should be dedicated to strengthening public education rather than to subsidizing private alternatives.' He also supports reduced standardized testing and expanded teacher autonomy. No statements on pre-K, Head Start, or government-funded childcare programs were found.

child_hunger.summary: No specific public position on SNAP, Summer EBT, school meals, or child nutrition programs has been found. Fritts' platform opposes new government spending while supporting elimination of the 4% grocery sales tax as broad-based cost relief.
child_hunger.details: Fritts has made eliminating Tennessee's 4% grocery sales tax a centerpiece of his fiscal platform, stating it would 'give relief to all Tennesseans.' His broader budget philosophy holds that 'budget requests should fund only core government functions, not new programs' and that 'public funds should go only to essentials: energy, water, waste, roads, and emergency services.' No direct statements on SNAP, Summer EBT, or federal child nutrition programs were found in campaign materials or media coverage through May 2026.

parental_support.summary: No specific public position on paid family leave, the child tax credit, or childcare costs has been found. Fritts' governing philosophy limits state government to core functions and explicitly opposes new spending programs.
parental_support.details: Fritts' platform does not address paid family leave, child tax credits, or childcare affordability in any reviewed campaign material or media coverage. His fiscal framework explicitly states that 'budget requests should fund only core government functions, not new programs' and criticizes 'corporate welfare' in state budgeting. His 'No bias in economy or education' platform plank states he would 'end government picking winners and losers' and oppose 'arbitrary criteria for grants, loans, scholarships, or incentives.' No legislative votes or statements on family economic support policies were identified in the 2026 House session or campaign trail.

name: Lauren Pinkston
bio: Independent gubernatorial candidate. Former Lipscomb University professor with a detailed family-economic platform — only candidate proposing redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship funds to early childhood ed and employer on-site daycare.
photo_credit: Direct headshot URL not found; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Pinkston strongly supports expanding affordable early childhood education, proposing to redirect Tennessee's Education Freedom Scholarship budget increases toward pre-K and to support businesses that offer on-site daycare. This position was reaffirmed in a March 2026 podcast interview.
early_childhood_ed.details: Pinkston's platform states she 'strongly supports shifting Tennessee increased budget Education Freedom Scholarships to early childhood education funds, as well as any budget measures that will expand the number of affordable early childhood education opportunities for families in Tennessee.' She specifically proposes these funds 'support businesses that offer on-site daycare,' framing the investment as growing the workforce, expanding the economy through dual-income households, and relieving financial pressure on young families. In a March 2026 interview on The Loyal Opposition podcast, she reiterated her priority of 'shifting focus from vouchers to early childhood and workplace childcare.' This is the most detailed early childhood education proposal among the gubernatorial candidates.

child_hunger.summary: Pinkston explicitly opposes SNAP benefit restrictions — arguing they harm local grocers and raise costs for middle-class families — and supports exploring removal of the grocery tax. Her platform positions her as the most opposed to SNAP purchase restrictions among the gubernatorial candidates.
child_hunger.details: Pinkston's platform states: 'Lauren opposes restrictions that would block SNAP benefits from being used for certain foods like snacks or sodas. These restrictions would harm local grocers and drive up food costs for middle-class families.' She also supports 'exploring the fiscal viability of removing the grocery tax in Tennessee, while protecting the stability of the state budget.' Her income incentive policy proposes restructuring public assistance to eliminate 'benefit cliffs' where recipients lose benefits upon earning more. No specific post-April 2026 statement responding to Tennessee's SNAP junk food waiver approval (slated to take effect July 2026) was found in reviewed sources.

parental_support.summary: Pinkston supports restructuring public assistance to eliminate benefit cliffs that penalize working parents, and proposes channeling early childhood education funding toward businesses offering on-site daycare as a childcare cost-relief measure for dual-income families.
parental_support.details: Pinkston's platform ties parental financial support to two main mechanisms: first, redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship budget growth to early childhood education and employer on-site daycare, described as a way to 'relieve financial pressure on growing families with young children'; second, working with the Department of Human Services to eliminate 'benefit cliffs' that create disincentives to work for families receiving public assistance. She also supports protecting collective bargaining rights, framing strong workplaces as foundational to 'stronger families, communities, and local economies.' No standalone paid family leave mandate or child tax credit proposal was found in her platform materials, and no specific response to the federal Working Families Tax Cuts was found through May 2026.

name: Jerri Green
bio: Democratic primary frontrunner running a coalition campaign rooted in West Tennessee. Focused on healthcare, education, and rural-urban balance.
photo_credit: Green for Governor official campaign website

early_childhood_ed.summary: Green supports universal pre-K, a dedicated childcare and early education fund, expanded home visiting programs, and robust special education investment. Her campaign homepage explicitly lists 'Affordable child care' as a core commitment alongside paid family leave. Her Memphis City Council record includes personally putting 'more kids in pre-K and youth programming.'
early_childhood_ed.details: Green's campaign homepage (greenforgovernor.com) states: 'Paid family leave. Affordable child care. A real living wage. Because families deserve more than survival — they deserve stability and dignity.' Her About page documents her Memphis City Council record: 'Jerri has increased funding for first responders, pushed legislation to crack down on neglectful landlords, put more kids in pre-K and youth programming, and reduced violent crime.' Her full platform (when accessible) commits to: 'invest in universal pre-K, special education, and rural schools'; 'start a dedicated childcare and early education fund, to include investments in afterschool and summer care programming for households making less than $75K a year'; and as a Day One priority: 'Use $50 Million of TANF funding to clear the waitlist for every family, ensuring no parent has to choose between a paycheck and their child.' She has a Special Education Equity Fund proposal and a 'Teach Every Student' fellowship to recruit special education teachers.

child_hunger.summary: Green explicitly opposes cuts to SNAP and has pledged to use state resources to combat child food insecurity, stating that one in five Tennessee children goes to bed hungry. She has a documented record of taking concrete action during federal SNAP disruptions — including championing free bus passes during the 2025 government shutdown that disrupted SNAP benefits.
child_hunger.details: At a February 2026 campaign event, Green stated: '1 in 5 kids right now in the state of Tennessee goes to bed hungry; our governor and government won't step up, and we can change that,' and pledged to 'budget to fund those in need of SNAP/EBT benefits who were affected by the Big Beautiful Bill.' Her About page notes she 'championed free bus passes to provide support during the federal government shutdown and cuts to SNAP benefits' as a Memphis City Council action. Her platform explicitly includes a commitment to 'lift families out of poverty — not punish them with cruel cuts to SNAP or housing aid' and to eliminate the state grocery tax. Context: Tennessee Lookout (June 16, 2026) reported ~100,000 Tennesseans lost SNAP benefits since the OBBB took effect in July 2025, with enrollment dropping from 696,000 to 597,890.

parental_support.summary: Green supports expanded paid family and medical leave, affordable childcare, and a Day One commitment to use $50 million in TANF funds to clear Tennessee's childcare waitlist, as well as a free diaper stipend program and elimination of the diaper and menstrual product tax.
parental_support.details: Green's platform commits to 'expand paid family and medical leave,' 'make quality childcare more accessible and affordable,' and as a Day One priority: 'Use $50 Million of TANF funding to clear the waitlist for every family, ensuring no parent has to choose between a paycheck and their child.' She pledges to 'create a stipend program to offer free diapers to low-income parents' and 'end the tax on diapers and menstrual products.' At a February 2026 campaign appearance she stated: 'We can create subsidies for people who are below the poverty level to help get them quality, affordable childcare and make sure those childcare centers are paying their workers a living wage.' These positions were reiterated at an April 2026 Grundy County rally.

name: Dr. Carnita Atwater
bio: Memphis community advocate making her second gubernatorial run. Known for community development work in the New Chicago neighborhood.

early_childhood_ed.summary: No specific early childhood education or pre-K policy position has been published or stated on record by Dr. Carnita Atwater as of May 2026; her campaign themes center on equity and community empowerment without a dedicated early childhood education plank.
early_childhood_ed.details: Atwater's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response describes a broad vision of equity, justice, and community-driven governance but does not include specific proposals for universal pre-K, Head Start expansion, or early childhood development programs. OnTheIssues.org lists 'no stance on record' for Families and Children policy. In an April 2026 candidate comparison published by The Redemption Project, Atwater 'did not provide direct responses' to policy questionnaires. Her campaign website was inaccessible (503 error) at time of research.

child_hunger.summary: Atwater has expressed a commitment to addressing food insecurity in underserved communities, specifically proposing 'portable food satellites in every food desert across Tennessee' to ensure no child goes hungry, but has not published a detailed SNAP, Summer EBT, or child nutrition program position.
child_hunger.details: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Atwater described a vision in which she 'would place portable food satellites in every food desert across Tennessee to assure that no child goes to sleep hungry.' No specific stance on SNAP funding levels, Summer EBT participation, or school meal programs has been identified in public statements or campaign materials reviewed. OnTheIssues.org lists 'no stance on record' for Welfare and Poverty policy. Atwater did not respond to The Redemption Project's April 2026 gubernatorial candidate questionnaire.

parental_support.summary: No specific positions on paid family leave, child tax credits, or structured childcare cost relief have been published by Dr. Carnita Atwater as of May 2026; her parental support focus centers on poverty reduction, child safety, and community investment.
parental_support.details: Atwater's Ballotpedia survey responses and available public record do not include explicit proposals on paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or child tax credit expansion. Her broader platform emphasizes reducing poverty, addressing housing disparities, supporting foster care reform, and fighting for children's safety from gun violence. OnTheIssues.org lists 'no stance on record' for Families and Children policy. No campaign materials or press coverage between April and May 2026 introduced new parental support policy positions.
